message:
refactor(install): share registration, and pass the version instead of compiling it in

The updater needed to register an installation, and the obvious shortcut --
re-run the installed GNLinkSetup.exe with a register-only flag -- turns out to
be the one option that cannot work. GNLinkSetup.exe is not in the payload list
and is copied separately, so after an update the copy on disk is still the
previous build. Its DisplayVersion is a compile-time constant, so registering
through it would write the old version into the very key read_installed_version
reads, and every later "is this newer" decision would be measured against a
lie.

So registration moves into a unit both binaries link, and the version becomes
an argument. The installer passes its constant; the updater will pass the
version off a verified manifest.

Failures are reported by step rather than swallowed. The installer today shows
a message box when service registration fails and then returns success anyway;
a caller that cannot tell a complete registration from a partial one has no
basis for deciding whether to roll back, so this stops at the first failure and
names it, keeping the list of what did complete.

Rollback restores a snapshot captured before the swap, not the new version.
Files going back to the previous build while the registry claims the new one is
the same poisoning arrived at from the other direction. A snapshot of "nothing
was registered" removes the key rather than writing blanks.

Two corrections while here. The comment claiming the swap is all-or-nothing now
says what is true: the FILE swap is, and the update as a whole is a sequence of
recoverable steps, not a transaction -- several files plus four separate system
facts cannot be made atomic. And request_process_stop now holds its verified
handle open for the whole call; verifying and then closing left a window where
the PID could be reused before the WM_CLOSE went out.

Tested under HKCU with netsh, the SCM and the Start menu recorded rather than
performed. Afterwards the real uninstall key still reads 0.2.104 and
GNLinkSecureInput is still running.

qwinsta: console active, rdp-tcp listening. 45 checks; installer relinks clean.
No real service, firewall rule or shortcut was created.
